text:
miguel: heads-up — trying to use the JS SDK inside a Next.js middleware (Vercel Edge runtime) and build fails with `ReferenceError: process is not defined` and later `require is not defined`. Minimal repro:
```js
import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference';
export function middleware(req) {
  const c = createClient();
}
```
I'm on SDK v0.9.2, Next 13.5, standard Vercel setup.

emily: that lines up with edge constraints — middleware must be ESM and no Node polyfills. Our CJS bundle pulls in `process` and maybe `crypto` shims. Do you see stack traces referencing `bindings` or `node:crypto`?

miguel: stack points to a small wrapper that does `const isBrowser = typeof process === 'undefined' ? false : process.env.__XXX` — so yeah the package checks `process`. Build fails at Vercel's bundler step with `require is not defined` too.

raj: short-term workaround: avoid top-level imports of the main CJS entry. Use dynamic import of an ESM edge entrypoint (we added an edge-friendly build in mainline, but it wasn't published in your version). Example that worked for me:
```js
export async function middleware(req) {
  const { createEdgeClient } = await import('@redwood/inference/edge');
  const c = createEdgeClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY });
  // use c...
}
```
This keeps the bundler from pulling in Node-only deps at build time.

emily: note: Vercel's Edge runtime may not expose `crypto.subtle` in older runtimes — our SDK expects webcrypto. Add a runtime guard: `if (typeof crypto?.subtle === 'undefined') { /* small fallback or throw descriptive error */ }`.

miguel: dynamic import got past the build, thanks. But TS tooling in dev (next dev) now errors: `Cannot use import statement outside a module` for the dynamic import guess? Also missing types — `@redwood/inference/edge` has no d.ts in my node_modules for v0.9.2.

raj: for the TS issue, two options: 1) Add a tiny ambient declaration in your app: `// global.d.ts\ndeclare module '@redwood/inference/edge' { export function createEdgeClient(opts?: any): any }`  OR 2) add a triple-slash reference if you maintain typed defs. We'll push proper types in the next release.

ci-bot: deploy started: vercel/production (miguel) — build logs: https://vercel.link/abclog 

emily: I'll open a PR to publish a named ESM export + bundled types under the `exports` field so consumers can `import { createEdgeClient } from '@redwood/inference/edge'` cleanly. For now add to the docs: "Edge runtime checklist":
- avoid sync top-level `require`
- use dynamic `import()` for the edge entrypoint
- ensure webcrypto available or guard
- add ambient module defs for older TS projects

miguel: can you also add a note about fetch + AbortSignal semantics? Our auth middleware retries and passes a signal into SDK fetch wrapper and on Edge that threw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'aborted')` — probably because polyfill mismatch.

raj: good call — I'll add that to the checklist: prefer `signal` from `req.signal` (edge) and our SDK will accept it, but avoid Node `AbortController` shims. Also adding a tiny example in sample-apps middleware example.

emily: thanks — I'll create the docs PR + small sample app update in `devex/sample-apps/next-edge` with the dynamic import pattern and a typed `global.d.ts` snippet.

miguel: sweet, that should unblock us. :thumbsup:
